# Relimie - Full Documentation

## SECTION: RELIMIE

## Mindful Enjoyment, Not Sacrifice

Relimie isn't just about quitting drinking, and it's more than an alcohol tracker: it's a mindful drinking companion for those who enjoy a drink but want to prevent their habits from becoming an addiction — without the guilt or judgment that often comes with tracking.

In Relimie, everything revolves around your **[Personal Baseline](faq.html#what-is-a-personal-baseline)** (which is why we call our method "baseline-drinking"). Instead of a rigid daily limit that feels like a failure if you miss it, your baseline is a long-term anchor. Life happens: some nights you'll have an extra glass, others you won't drink at all. What matters is the trend. Over time, your habits naturally gravitate back toward your goal.

Tapping your glowing **Orb** shows you where you stand at a glance: **Green** — you're comfortably within your baseline; **Gold** — you're slightly over your limit; **Red** — you should consider pausing for a few days to bring your average back in line. The green signs also show you how many drinks you have avoided so far. You can use this information to adjust your baseline down and **[reduce your consumption step by step](faq.html#how-does-the-baseline-help-me-reduce-my-drinking)**, if you wish.

To help you **[choose your baseline](faq.html#how-do-i-choose-the-right-baseline)**, we provide data from WHO recommendations and average values for your country and gender. These serve as orientation until you find your personal values. Relimie also supports a variety of measurement units, so you can use those you understand best (like grams of pure alcohol or standard US units).

Keep in mind that while baseline-drinking is a powerful helper for controlling your behavior, it won't do the work for you. You need to put in the effort to stick to your baseline and log accurately. Since the baseline is based on aggregation, it needs some time to "kick in" as it collects data. Don't be discouraged if you don't see it change immediately, even though it becomes available right after onboarding.

Curious where baseline-drinking came from? It grew out of a single number and one person's struggle to stay in control — [read the story behind Relimie](story.html).


---

## SECTION: DIARY

## Connect the Dots: Why You Drink

Tracking numbers is just the start. Your alcohol diary is where you find the *[why](faq.html#what-is-relimies-philosophy)*.

By logging how you feel — before a drink, the morning after, or on a clear-headed day — you start to see the patterns that usually stay hidden. It's about spotting triggers and finding a way to stay ahead of them. The diary helps you understand the consequences and spot the moments when you need to take control.

**Contextual tags appear when you need them:**

- **Triggers** surface when you log alcohol (stress, boredom, social pressure)
- **After-Effects** wait for you the next morning (hangover, anxiety, clarity)
- **Sober Feelings** highlight the wins (productivity, pride, energy)

Inside the Analytics Hub, your most frequent tags are ranked against your drinking days — helping you anticipate the situations where you're most likely to slip, so you can stay ahead of them. And, of course, you can add your own tags in the settings menu.


---

## SECTION: LOGGING

## Logging without the Friction

Tracking shouldn't be a chore. Relimie is built to get you in and out in seconds, while automatically capturing the details that actually matter.

**Every entry adds up to your big picture:**

- **Alcohol** — Track the total pure alcohol consumed with each drink.
- **Spending** — See exactly what you're spending. Prices are preset based on your country's averages, but you can always **[adjust them](faq.html#how-do-i-enter-or-adjust-my-spending)** for a single drink or the whole day. Just long-press a drink in the list or the total amount at the bottom. Prices are also split between "home" and "outside" consumption for better accuracy.
- **Calories** — Each drink comes with predefined calorie counts so you can see the real impact on your fitness goals, not just the unit count. If you need to be exact, you can adjust these for any drink.

Relimie features a catalog of the most common drinks, and you can easily **[add your own](faq.html#can-i-create-my-own-drinks)**. To make adding new drinks as simple as possible, use the **AI Sparkle button**. It appears in the search bar whenever you enter a drink not found in the catalog. One tap will research and autofill the ABV and calories, so you never have to guess. Feel free to provide feedback if something doesn't work as expected — we’re always improving.

All of this data flows into your **Analytics Hub**, where daily entries become the insights that help you stay in control.

> 🎁 **And most importantly:** Logging your alcohol, calories, and spending is **[completely free](faq.html#is-relimie-free)**, along with the essential analytics to track them. You don't need a premium subscription to use these features for as long as you like!


---

## SECTION: ANALYTICS

## See Your Story. Own Your Data.

The **[Analytics Hub](faq.html#how-do-i-use-the-analytics-features)** turns your daily entries into a clear picture of your balance. Just swipe up from the Home Screen to see where you stand.

**What's inside:**

- **History** — Go back and forth in time.
- **Overview** — Your spending, caloric impact, and the ratio of clear days to drinking ones (available in the free version as well).
- **Habits** — A graphical overview of your drinking habits.
- **Trends** — Spot the specific days and times when you're most likely to drift off course.
- **Log** — Look back at any date to adjust entries, update notes, or refine how you felt.
- **Full-Screen Chart** — Turn your phone sideways for a full landscape view of your consumption over time, so a change in direction is easy to catch early.

**Private by Design:**

Your **[data never leaves your device](faq.html#is-my-data-private)**. When you want to, you can generate a **"Share My Story" PDF** to show progress to someone — without sharing your private journal notes. Or export a **JSON Backup** for your own analysis.

No cloud, no tracking, no third-party access. Ever.


---

## SECTION: CRAVINGS

## Cravings Breaker

## Breathe Through the Impulse

A craving doesn't ask for permission. It hits fast, and in those first 30 seconds, willpower alone can feel like it's not enough. But if you can disrupt that initial impulse, you give your brain the space it needs to step back and stay on track.

## Your Instant Circuit Breaker

**Long-press the Orb** on the Home Screen to trigger the **[Cravings Breaker](faq.html#what-is-the-cravings-breaker)** immediately. Your screen transforms into a calm, pulsing guide for the **4-7-8 Breathing Technique**. As you breathe, grounding quotes help anchor your focus and steady your mind until the urge passes.

## Turn a Challenge into a Win

When the cycle ends, Relimie prompts you to log a **Clear Day**. By turning a moment of resistance into a trackable achievement, you transform a difficult impulse into another brick in your streak. Every urge you ride out is proof of your progress — whether you're cutting back or taking on **[Dry January or Sober October](faq.html#can-i-use-relimie-for-dry-january-or-sober-october)**.

## See Your Body Bounce Back

Right on the breathing screen, a **Body Recovery Timeline** counts from your last drink and shows what your body tends to regain over time — from better sleep and energy in the first days to longer-term changes across a year. It's one more small reason to keep your streak going.

> 🎁 **Free for everyone:** The Body Recovery Timeline is available to every user at no cost.

If you have any ideas what else can help against the craving, let us know at [support@relimie.com]!

## SECTION: USER GUIDE

# Relimie - User Guide

Welcome to Relimie, your mindful companion for tracking alcohol consumption, analyzing your habits, and celebrating your sobriety milestones. This guide walks you through the core concepts of the app to help you make the most of your journey. For more detailed information, usage videos, and a deeper dive into our philosophy, please visit the **[Relimie website](https://relimie.github.io)**.

## Table of Contents
- [1. Personal Baseline](#1-personal-baseline)
- [2. Drinks Logging](#2-drinks-logging)
- [3. Blood Alcohol Estimate](#3-blood-alcohol-estimate)
- [4. Diary and Tags](#4-diary-and-tags)
- [5. Cravings and Breathing](#5-cravings-and-breathing)
- [6. Analytics Hub](#6-analytics-hub)
- [7. Data Export](#7-data-export)
- [8. Additional Features](#8-additional-features)
- [9. Relimie Premium](#9-relimie-premium)

## 1. Personal Baseline

### The Core Concept
Setting a **Personal Baseline** is the foundational step in understanding and managing your alcohol consumption. Instead of merely counting drinks, a baseline gives your tracking meaning by acting as your personalized long-term orientation point.

It is important to understand what a baseline *is* — and what it *isn't*. It is expressed as a daily alcohol amount, but it is **not a strict daily limit you must never cross**. Think of it more like a long-term average you are aiming to stay around. Some days you may drink a little more, some days less or not at all — that is perfectly normal. What matters is that over time, your consumption gravitates back toward, and ideally below, that middle value. The baseline is your compass, not a hard wall.

By setting this personal target, tracking becomes genuinely actionable: the app clearly shows you when you are running ahead of your pace, exactly how many recovery days you need to bring your average back in line, and how many drinks you've successfully avoided to protect your health.

### Establishing the Baseline
Your Personal Baseline is initially configured during the **Onboarding** process when you first launch the app. As your lifestyle and habits evolve, you can effortlessly adjust this limit at any time by navigating to **Settings -> Personalization** to redefine your pure alcohol ceiling.

### Determining Your Target
If you are unsure what a healthy baseline looks like, Relimie provides dynamic, science-based suggestions. These recommendations are aligned with the **World Health Organization (WHO)** guidelines. The app also contextualizes your target by comparing it against the median consumption levels tailored to your country's health data and adjusted for your gender. As your habits improve, pay attention to your actual consumption patterns: if you consistently find yourself drinking well below your current limit, that is a strong positive signal — consider revisiting **Settings → Personalization** to tighten your baseline to a lower value. Your ceiling should grow stricter as you grow stronger.

### Tracking Your Progress
Once your baseline is established, monitoring your adherence takes only moments. By tapping the glowing **Orb** on your Home Screen, you toggle into the **Baseline Trend View** — a second tap cycles you back to the standard display. This instantly visualizes whether you are under your limit or exactly how many recovery days you need to get back on track. The Orb's color signals your position at a glance: **green** when you are safely within your limit, **gold** when you are approaching it, and **red** when recovery days are needed. Note that on **past dates**, tapping the Orb does not cycle views — instead, it logs a "Clear Day" for that day if it has no entry recorded. For comprehensive, long-term macro-shifts, you can dive deeper into the **Trends** tab located inside the Analytics Hub.

---

## 2. Drinks Logging

### The Core Concept
Tracking your drinks accurately should be completely frictionless while still providing a wealth of data for your future self. Relimie goes beyond standard alcohol counting by capturing a holistic picture of your consumption's real-world impact. When you are ready to track, simply tap the **Add Drink** button on the Home Screen.

### Comprehensive Tracking
When you log a drink, you inherently log much more than just the alcohol. Relimie automatically calculates the **money spent** by estimating costs based on your country and your selected location context — you can choose between **"Home"** and **"Outside"** directly within the logging screen, since a drink at a bar typically costs significantly more than the same drink at home. If the auto-calculated summary price still doesn't match your actual bill, you can easily correct it by **long-pressing the Total Price** in the bottom summary bar to manually overwrite the final amount spent. Furthermore, the app actively counts the **calories** generated by your alcohol intake, providing another layer of health awareness.

### Navigating the Catalog and AI Assistance
Relimie stores a built-in catalog of pre-delivered standard drinks, but also allows you to securely save any number of your own custom drinks. To make navigating this growing catalog effortless, a dedicated **Search Bar** helps you find your drinks faster. Once you have typed a search term and no match is found, the **AI Sparkle button** automatically appears. Tapping this button prompts the system to research and autofill the correct Volume and ABV for your new drink. AI-assisted detection is available across all tiers, though the number of monthly lookups is tiered — **Trial** users receive a generous quota to explore the feature, while **Subscription** and **Lifetime Premium** holders enjoy higher limits. You also have total control over what is displayed: you can use the **(+) button** to define custom drinks manually, and you can use the **Organizing Dialog** to hide any catalog drinks you don't use, keeping your interface beautifully relevant to your lifestyle.

### Reviewing Your Statistics
All of this comprehensively collected data is gathered and visualized for you inside the **Analytics Hub**. You can open the Hub at any time by **swiping up** on the Home Screen, or by tapping the **grid icon** in the top corner of the screen. Inside, you'll find the **Consumption Overview**. This section breaks your logging down in explicit detail:
- **Money Spent:** You can track the precise financial impact of your habits by viewing your *Total Spent* over your entire tracking lifespan, alongside your *Avg Spent* (average daily cost). Furthermore, this financial data actively powers the insights in the **Trends** and **Habits** tabs, allowing you to evaluate if your monthly spending is safely decreasing or dangerously increasing compared to past months.
- **Calories Counted:** See exactly how drinking affects your diet by viewing your *Total Calories* and your daily *Avg Calories*.
- **Alcohol Volume:** The tab clearly tracks your total pure alcohol intake and the overall volume of standard drinks you've consumed.
This detailed breakdown ensures you maintain a holistic, immediate view of the financial and physical impacts of your consumption over time.

---

## 3. Blood Alcohol Estimate

### The Core Concept
After a night of drinking, the question that actually matters the next morning is not "how drunk am I" — it is "how long until this is out of my system". The Blood Alcohol Estimate answers exactly that. It takes the alcohol you logged for a day and estimates the blood alcohol level (in ‰) it would produce, then shows you how that value falls over the following hours. It is a recovery clock, never a green light.

### Opening the Estimator
On the Home Screen, a small **gauge button** sits in the corner beside the Orb. On any day where you have logged drinks — today or a past day — it lights up teal; on sober days and days with nothing logged it stays dimmed, because there is nothing to estimate. Tapping it opens the estimator as its own screen; you leave it again with the **X**, a swipe to the right, or your device's back gesture. The estimator is **completely free** — it is not part of Relimie Premium and never expires with your trial.

### Setting Your Body Weight
Blood alcohol depends heavily on how much body mass the alcohol distributes into, so the estimator needs your **body weight** before it can show you anything. The very first time you open it, the big value reads `–,–` and stays locked — Relimie deliberately refuses to guess, because an assumed weight would show a *lower* value and a *shorter* wait to anyone lighter than the assumption, which is the one direction this feature must never err in. Set your weight with the **− / +** buttons in the body card (in **kilograms**, between 40 and 150 kg) and tap **Save & estimate**. From then on the estimate appears immediately, and every tap on − / + updates it live. Your weight is stored on your device only, exactly like the rest of your data. Your **gender** is also used, since it changes how alcohol distributes in the body — it is shown in the same card for reference but is edited in **Settings → Personalization**, not here.

### Reading the Estimate
The top row tells you exactly what the estimate is based on: the total alcohol you logged for that day. Below it, the large ‰ value is the estimated blood alcohol level. The **hours slider** lets you scrub forward from your last drink of the day — up to 24 hours in half-hour steps — and watch the value fall until it reads fully cleared. Two rows underneath give you the summary at a glance: how long until the estimate drops **below 0.5 ‰**, and how long until it is **fully cleared**. Both of these are counted from your last drink of the day, so they stay put while you move the slider.

### How It Is Calculated
Relimie uses the **Widmark formula**: your logged grams of pure alcohol divided by your body weight times a distribution factor that depends on gender, with the alcohol then eliminated at a steady 0.15 ‰ per hour. The whole day's intake is treated as if it hit your blood at once, and no deduction is made for the portion your body breaks down before it ever reaches the bloodstream. Every one of those choices — plus rounding all durations up to the next five minutes — deliberately points the same way: **a higher number and a longer wait** than you are likely to actually have. That is the only direction that cannot hurt someone acting on the result.

### What This Number Is Not
**This is an estimate, not a measurement.** Your real blood alcohol depends on many factors this calculation cannot know — what and when you ate, how the drinks were spread across the evening, medication, your health and your individual metabolism — and it can be considerably higher than what is shown. **Never use this number to decide whether you are fit to drive, to work, or to take medication.** If you are in any doubt, don't.

---

## 4. Diary and Tags

### The Core Concept
Understanding *why* you drink is vastly more important than simply counting *what* you drink. The Diary and Tagging system is intentionally designed to build the emotional and situational context directly around your numerical data.

### Documenting the Emotional Context
Emotional context is crucial for identifying behavioral triggers. By logging your emotional state before drinking, how you feel the day after a heavy session, or the positive energy you experience during a sober streak, you build a roadmap of your psychology. You can seamlessly reach your daily journal directly by tapping the **Log** button right on the Home Screen. Furthermore, you can also access it automatically after logging a new drink, by tapping any specific chronological day inside your Diary, or simply by swiping the date layout on the Home Screen. For **Premium** users, tapping directly on any entry in the Diary History acts as a quick-edit shortcut, jumping straight to that day's journal without navigating away from the Diary view.

### Contextual Tagging System
Relimie offers fast, contextual emotional tags to categorize your days. The app automatically detects your situation and surfaces only the most relevant category — no manual selection required. **Triggers** (like stressed, bored, or facing social pressure) appear when you log alcohol, **After-Effects** (such as hangover, anxiety, or guilt) are available the day after drinking, and **Sober Feelings** (like feeling productive or great) are highlighted on clean days. You can perfectly match your personal psychological footprint by creating and managing custom, user-defined tags through the **Settings** menu.

### Recognizing Patterns
Over time, this emotional data becomes your strongest tool. Inside the Analytics Hub under the **Habits** section, Relimie actively re-ranks your most frequently used tags up against your consumption days. This automatically generates a "Top Reasons You Drink" list, allowing you to anticipate and actively avoid specific situational triggers.

---

## 5. Cravings and Breathing

### The Core Concept
When a sudden urge or craving to drink hits, sheer willpower often isn't enough. Disrupting the immediate impulse gives your rational brain a crucial moment to catch up and regain control, significantly reducing the probability of an unwanted relapse.

### Riding Out the Impulse
By long-pressing the Orb on Today's date, you trigger an immediate psychological circuit breaker directly on the Home Screen. The screen transforms into a calm, expanding and contracting visual that guides you through the proven **4-7-8 Breathing Technique** — inhaling for 4 seconds, holding for 7, and exhaling for 8. A card below the visual keeps you company through the cycle: it opens on your Regeneration Timeline, and a single tap flips it to a grounding citation to help anchor your focus. Once the breathing cycle completes, the app surfaces a prompt to log a **"Clear Day"** — a positive reinforcement step that turns the act of resisting a craving into a trackable achievement on your sober streak.

### Your Regeneration Timeline
The breathing screen does more than guide your breath — it also shows how your body bounces back. The card below the breathing orb **opens directly on your personal Regeneration Timeline**: a series of science-based milestones — **Day 1** (alcohol cleared), **Day 7** (rest returns), **Day 30** (body resets), **Day 90** (fully adjusted), **Day 180** (systems stronger), and **Day 365** (the one-year milestone). It highlights how far you've come based on the time since your last logged drink and what the next milestone brings. Tap the **?** for the full breakdown of each stage, or **tap the card itself to flip it over** for a grounding citation. This is general orientation, not medical advice — actual recovery varies from person to person and depends on factors like overall health, age, and lifestyle.

---

## 6. Analytics Hub

### The Core Concept
The Analytics Hub is where your daily inputs are transformed into actionable, long-term insights, allowing you to view your overarching progress and behavior shifts clearly. You can open it at any time by **swiping up** on the Home Screen, or by tapping the **grid icon** in the top corner of the screen.

### Visualizing Your Lifespan
The hub provides a complete snapshot of your tracking lifespan. Inside, you can review your **Consumption Overview** to see your daily average spending, total caloric impact, and your overall ratio of sober days versus drinking days. The **Streaks System** cleanly highlights your defining milestones, placing your longest ever sober streak in perspective against your longest heavy drinking period. Through sweeping visual charts, the **Trends and Habits** sections allow you to verify if your consumption and spending are currently trending safely downward, and pinpoint exactly which days of the week or months of the year leave you most vulnerable to relapse.

### Reviewing Consumption History
Below your overview metrics, the Hub hosts your complete **Consumption History**. This chronologically ordered ledger allows you to easily review all past entries. More importantly, tapping directly on the history summary opens a date picker, allowing you to seamlessly navigate back to any specific previous date on the Home Screen. From there, you can effortlessly adjust logged drinks, amend your diary notes, or refine your emotional tags entirely retroactively.

### The Landscape Consumption Chart
For a focused, full-width view of your trends, simply **rotate your phone to landscape while on the Home Screen** — Relimie opens a dedicated **Consumption Chart**. Switch the metric between **Units**, **Money**, and **Calories**, and the timeframe between **Daily**, **Weekly**, and **Monthly**. On the daily alcohol view, the chart also overlays your **Baseline** and your rolling **Average**, so you can see at a glance whether your intake is trending below your target over time. The landscape chart is a **Premium** feature — available during your free trial and with Relimie Premium.

---

## 7. Data Export

### The Core Concept
Your sobriety journey is intimately private. While there may be times you need to share your progress with a medical professional or securely back up your history, Relimie ensures you retain complete ownership over your data by defaulting to a private, offline-first architecture.

### Sharing and Protecting Your History
To share your milestones with a therapist, doctor, or sponsor, you can generate a **"Share My Story" PDF Export** native to the Hub. This creates a beautifully rendered report of your critical metrics. To protect your privacy, it omits your deeply personal journal prose, while still including your emotional **tags** — so your behavioral patterns remain visible without exposing your private thoughts. Additionally, the **Raw JSON Backup** tool exports your entire application profile — including all logs, catalog, and tag configurations — into a portable file. This is ideal for deep-diving into your own data using an external tool or a **Gen AI assistant** to surface patterns that go beyond the built-in analytics.

---

## 8. Additional Features

While tracking and analyzing form the core of Relimie, the app also includes several utility features to further support your journey:
- **Alcohol Unit Customization**: Relimie can display your consumption in the unit system that feels most natural to you. Navigate to **Settings → Personalization** to choose between Grams of pure alcohol, Milliliters, or Standard Drinks calibrated to the **US**, **UK**, or **Australian** definitions.
- **Multilingual Support**: Relimie is fully localized to ensure you can interact with your health data in your native tongue. Currently, the app natively supports three languages: English, German, and Russian.
- **Daily Reminders**: To help you build a consistent tracking habit, you can enable a daily reminder notification through the **Settings** menu. This gentle nudge ensures you never forget to check in and log your daily emotional state.
- **Guided Tours**: Several screens carry a small **question-mark button** next to their title — on the Home screen you'll find it at the right end of the month row, just above the dates. Tap it and a short interactive tour walks you through that page, pointing out the non-obvious gestures and shortcuts (like long-pressing the Orb or swiping between views). Tours never start on their own and never get in your way: they run only when you ask, they cover only the page you're on, and you can replay one as often as you like. Tours are available on the **Home**, **Log Drinks** and **Check-in** screens.

---

## 9. Relimie Premium

To respect our users, the foundational tracking capabilities of Relimie are perpetually free. However, access to deep macro-analytics, unlimited historical reflections, and advanced AI utilities are part of the **Relimie Premium** experience.

### The 20-Logging-Day Free Trial
When you first start using Relimie, you are automatically granted a **20-Logging-Day Free Trial** that unlocks every premium feature. Only days with real content count toward these 20 days — a day where you log a drink, write a diary note, or add a tag. Pure sober days (a clean day with no drink and no diary entry) do **not** count, so marking sober days never uses up your trial. This gives you ample, fair time to explore the app at your own pace without feeling rushed.

### Core Free Tier (Always Free)
After your 20 logging days expire, you retain perpetual access to the most vital tools, completely for free:
- Unlimited daily logging of pre-delivered standard drinks.
- Full access to the interactive Home Screen Orb and Quick Actions (Log/Sober).
- The 4-7-8 Deep Breathing mindful exercise and your Regeneration Timeline.
- The Blood Alcohol Estimate on any day with logged drinks.
- Your sober streaks remaining visible on the Home Screen.
- Read-only access to your full historical Diary.

### Relimie Premium Features
Upgrading to **Relimie Premium** permanently unlocks (or continues) the following capabilities:
- **Advanced Orb Navigation**: Full access to the Baseline Trend View, allowing you to instantly visualize your distance to your target limit.
- **Diary & Reflection Writing**: The ability to write new journal entries and attach emotional tags to new days. After your trial expires, the Diary becomes read-only on the free tier.
- **Complete Customization**: AI-assisted drink creation, manual drink overrides, and expanding your personal drink catalog natively.
- **Deep Reflection**: Navigating backward through your full chronological ledger and using direct-editing shortcuts directly from the Diary.
- **Analytics & Exporting**: Permanent access to the powerful `Analytics`, `Trends`, and `Habits` tabs inside the Hub, the full-screen landscape Consumption Chart, along with the ability to generate PDF "Share My Story" reports and Raw JSON backups.

### Pricing Models
Upgrades are securely managed through your device's native app store. You can select the plan that best fits your lifestyle:
- **Monthly Subscription**: Auto-renewing, billed monthly.
- **Annual Subscription**: Auto-renewing, billed once per year.
- **Lifetime Purchase**: A one-time purchase granting access to all current premium features for the lifetime of the application.
- **Promo Codes**: If you have a promotional Apple Offer Code, you can seamlessly apply it directly through the "Redeem Code" link located in the app's Info menu.

### What is Relimie's philosophy?
We don't believe that just logging your drinks and staring at charts tells you anything new or actually changes your behavior. What makes the difference is having a **system to act on the data**. That system is simple, and we call it **[baseline-drinking](guide.html#1-personal-baseline)**: instead of a daily limit you pass or fail, you work from a long-term baseline (your normal, averaged over time), and the app gently nudges you back toward it and helps you step it down over time.

Just as important, the numbers alone don't explain *why* you drink. It matters to understand the **reasons** behind a drink, the **consequences** the next day, and how you **feel** — including the positive feelings on sober days. That's why Relimie comes with an **[alcohol diary and tag system](guide.html#3-diary-and-tags)** that captures this context right alongside your data.

Relimie is built to support **mindful, moderate drinking and the sober-curious approach** — no guilt, no preaching, and no requirement to quit. But it works just as well if quitting altogether is your goal: there the diary is especially valuable, helping you understand the reasons behind an urge and see how to avoid the situations that trigger it.

One honest note: Relimie can't guarantee that you'll reach your goals — that part is on you. The app can only provide the support and the system to make it easier; following through is your responsibility.

### What is a Personal Baseline?
Your **Personal Baseline** is a long-term anchor for your drinking. By default it's expressed as a daily amount of **pure alcohol in grams**, but you're not tied to that — on the **Settings → Personalization** page you can define and view it in whatever units feel natural to you: grams of pure alcohol, standard **US**, **UK**, or **Australian** units, or even an amount of your favorite type of drink. It is **not** a strict daily limit you must never cross. Think of it as a long-term average you aim to stay around — some days a little more, some days less or none at all. What matters is the trend over time.

There are two ways to follow your progress against it:
- **Tap the Orb** on the [Home Screen](guide.html#1-personal-baseline) to see your baseline trend visualized in color at a glance: **Green** (comfortably within your baseline), **Gold** (slightly over), or **Red** (consider pausing for a few days to bring your average back in line).
- Open the **Trends** section of the [Analytics Hub](guide.html#5-analytics-hub) for your "Target Progress," which calculates exactly how much sober buffer you have left or how many sober days you need to return to your baseline.

### How do I choose the right baseline?
Setting your baseline for the very first time is the tricky part, because most people honestly don't know what number to put there. So Relimie helps you start. For many countries we show reference values based on your **country and gender** — and where that data isn't available, we fall back to a worldwide average. You get two reference points: the **WHO recommendation** (a health-based guideline) and the **average** (roughly what people around you actually drink). If you have no idea where to begin, just start with the **average for your country and gender**.

From there you don't need to get it perfect. As you keep logging, Relimie shows how your real average consumption compares to the baseline you chose and suggests how to adjust it. Depending on your drinking habits, give it a few weeks to settle — the baseline needs some data before the picture becomes clear. A good sign to lower it: if you consistently drink well below your current baseline, tighten it a little — your target can grow stricter as you grow stronger. You can change it anytime under **Settings → Personalization**, and all of this stays on your device.

### How does the baseline help me reduce my drinking?
This is the core of how Relimie works. If reducing is your goal, the aim is simple to state: **push your baseline down over time, and consistently stay within it.** The two feed each other — staying within a baseline earns you the room to lower it, and a lower baseline pulls your habits down with it.

The **baseline trend** (the colored Orb and the Trends view) is what guides those adjustments honestly:
- If you're **consistently Gold or Red**, you were probably a little too optimistic when you set it. That's okay — be honest with yourself and **adjust the baseline up** to a level you can actually hold, then start working down from there.
- If you're **consistently Green** with a comfortable buffer built up (for example, around 500 g of pure alcohol below your baseline, or the equivalent in your chosen units), that's your signal to **adjust the baseline down** a notch.

Repeat that loop — hold the line, then tighten it — and your drinking genuinely comes down step by step. Just remember the app only **suggests and shows**: it gives you the system and honest feedback, but logging accurately and following through is on you.

### Can I use Relimie for Dry January or Sober October?
Absolutely. Relimie is a natural companion for **Dry January**, **Sober October**, or any sober stretch you set yourself. Mark each day sober with a single tap on the Orb, and Relimie turns the whole month into a clear streak you can watch grow. The [Analytics Hub](guide.html#5-analytics-hub) shows your run of sober days at a glance, the **Body Recovery Timeline** counts what your body regains along the way, and the [Cravings Breaker](cravings.html) is there for the evenings when an old habit pushes back. Because the app works from a long-term baseline rather than a hard rule, it doesn't treat a single slip as failure — you just pick the streak back up. When the challenge ends, your alcohol diary and trends help you decide what to carry forward into more mindful, moderate drinking the rest of the year.

### How do I use the analytics features?
Open the **Analytics Hub** by swiping up from the Home Screen or tapping the grid icon. Inside you'll find: **Overview** (daily average spending, calories, and your ratio of sober to drinking days — free), **Habits** (a graphical view of your patterns), **Trends** (the specific days and times you're most likely to drift off course), **History/Log** (revisit any past date to adjust entries), and a **chronological heatmap**. Rotate your phone to landscape on the Home Screen to open a full-screen **Consumption Chart** (Premium); on tablets, which stay in portrait, you can open the same chart from a button on the **Consumption History** in the Hub. When you want to, you can export a **"Share My Story" PDF** (without your private notes) or a full **JSON backup** — all without your data ever leaving the device.

### What is the Cravings Breaker?
Sometimes an urge to drink shows up for no big reason at all — often it's just an old habit, like reaching for a drink on a Friday evening. In those moments you don't need willpower for hours; usually a few minutes of something else to occupy your mind is enough for the urge to pass. That's where Relimie's **[Cravings Breaker](cravings.html)** comes in handy.

**Long-press the Orb** on the [Home Screen](guide.html#1-personal-baseline) to open it. The Cravings Breaker guides you through a 4-7-8 breathing exercise to calm down, with a few inspirational quotes to steady your focus until the moment passes. Flip the quote card and you'll also see your **Body Recovery Timeline** — what your body has been regaining since your last drink — as one more bit of motivation to stay sober.

### Can I create my own drinks?
Yes. Relimie ships with a catalog of preset drinks, but you can add your own in seconds. Type what you're having into the search bar, and if there's no match the **AI Sparkle button** appears — tap it and Relimie researches and fills in the right volume, ABV, and calories for you. AI-assisted creation is available on all plans, with monthly limits that scale by tier.

### How do I log past days (drinks and sober days)?
For recent days, swipe left on the horizontal **date picker** on the [Home Screen](guide.html#1-personal-baseline) to move back in time. On a past day, tap **Add Drink** to log a drink, or simply **tap the Orb** to mark that day as sober. For dates farther back, open the **Analytics Hub** and tap the [Chronological Heatmap](guide.html#5-analytics-hub) to jump to any date.

Logging your sober days matters just as much as your drinks — the baseline is only accurate if both are recorded. If you mostly open the app on days you drink, the sober days in between can pile up, and entering them one by one is a chore. Relimie makes it quick:
- **Tap the Orb** on any past day that has no entry yet to log it as a sober day.
- To fill a whole stretch at once, go to the most recent day you missed and **long-press the Orb**. A dialog appears asking if you want to mark every day sober back to your last logged entry — confirm, and the entire gap is filled in one step.

### How do I enter or adjust my spending?
You have two ways to adjust prices. To change the standard price of a specific drink globally, **long-press the drink card** in the catalog. If your total for the day doesn't match the automatic sum (e.g., due to a discount or shared bill), you can **long-press the Total Price** in the bottom summary bar on the [Logger Screen](guide.html#2-drinks-logging) to manually adjust the final daily amount.

### Is Relimie free?
Logging your drinks, money, and calories is always free, with no paywall on the basics — and so are the interactive Orb, the 4-7-8 breathing exercise, and the Body Recovery Timeline. The deeper analytics and the full diary live in **Relimie Premium**, and your first 20 logged days are free to explore them, so you can decide at your own pace. (Only days with real content count toward those 20 — pure sober days never use up your trial.)

### Is my data private?
Completely. Everything stays on your device: **no account, no email, no cloud, no third-party analytics, and no cookies.** The only network feature is optional AI drink creation, which sends just your short text description (plus your country/currency setting) to generate the drink — nothing personal leaves your phone. You can export a clean PDF report or a full backup whenever you like. See our [Privacy Policy](privacy.html) for the full details.

## ARTICLE: Promille Calculator: Blood Alcohol and How Long Until You're Sober

# Promille Calculator: Blood Alcohol and How Long Until You're Sober

The morning after, the question that actually matters is rarely "how drunk was I". It is "how much is still in me, and how long until it is gone". A promille calculator answers that with arithmetic, and the arithmetic is genuinely simple: one formula from 1932, two numbers about your body, and one rate at which your liver works.

What follows is that calculation, running live below, followed by an honest account of what it can and cannot tell you. There is no secret here worth guarding. The formula is a century old and any search engine will hand it to you. What is worth saying out loud is how far you should trust the number it produces, because most calculators present a result to two decimal places and leave you to assume that means precision.

This is not medical advice, and it is never a fitness-to-drive test. More on why that matters below.

(An interactive blood-alcohol calculator is embedded here on the web page: it takes grams of pure alcohol, body weight, gender and hours since the last drink, and returns the estimated per mille value, the peak, the time until below 0.5 permille and the time until fully cleared.)

## First, how many grams did you actually drink?

The calculator asks for grams of pure alcohol rather than "two beers", and that is deliberate. A small strong drink and a large weak one can hold exactly the same amount of alcohol, so grams are the only unit that lets you add an evening up.

Getting from a glass to grams takes one multiplication: volume in millilitres, times the strength as a decimal, times 0.8 (the density of ethanol). A 500 ml beer at 5% is 500 × 0.05 × 0.8 = 20 grams. Here is what common servings come to.

| Drink | Typical serving | Pure alcohol (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Small glass of wine | 125 ml (12%) | ~12 g |
| Standard glass of wine | 175 ml (12%) | ~17 g |
| Large glass of wine | 250 ml (13%) | ~26 g |
| Bottled beer | 330 ml (5%) | ~13 g |
| Pint of lager or ale | 568 ml (5%) | ~22 g |
| Single spirit | 25 ml (40%) | ~8 g |
| Double spirit | 50 ml (40%) | ~16 g |

Add up everything from the day and you have the number the calculator wants. This is also the step people get wrong most often, because it relies on remembering both what you drank and how large the pours were, several hours after the fact.

## The formula behind the number

The calculation is the [**Widmark formula**](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_alcohol_content), published by the Swedish chemist Erik Widmark in 1932 and still the basis of forensic blood alcohol estimation today:

**c = A / (m × r)**

- **c** is the blood alcohol concentration in per mille (‰)
- **A** is the grams of pure alcohol you drank
- **m** is your body mass in kilograms
- **r** is the distribution factor

The distribution factor is the part that needs explaining. Alcohol dissolves in water, not fat, so it spreads through the watery part of your body rather than all of it. **r** is the fraction of your body mass that alcohol actually distributes into. Because body composition differs on average between men and women, the standard values are **0.7 for men** and **0.6 for women**. Relimie uses **0.65** when gender is unset or recorded as other, which is the midpoint: it does not guess a body composition, and it errs neither systematically high nor low.

So for an 80 kg man who drank three half-litre beers, that is 60 grams of alcohol:

**60 / (80 × 0.7) = 1.07 ‰**

The same 60 grams in a 60 kg woman gives 60 / (60 × 0.6) = 1.67 ‰. Same drinks, a very different number, which is the single most useful thing the formula shows you.

## How long until it is gone

Your body then clears alcohol at a roughly constant rate, regardless of how much is in there. That is unusual, and it is why the wait is so much longer than people expect: the level comes down in a straight line, not a curve that drops off quickly at first.

The rate sits somewhere around **0.15 ‰ per hour** for most people, which is the value used here. From 1.07 ‰, that is 1.07 / 0.15 = about **7 hours and 10 minutes** to reach zero. Someone who stopped drinking at 1 a.m. is still not clear at 8 a.m.

Nothing meaningfully speeds this up. Coffee, a cold shower, fresh air, exercise, a large breakfast and a night's sleep all change how awake you feel, and none of them change the rate at which your liver metabolises ethanol. Feeling fine and being clear are two different states, and the gap between them is precisely where people get into trouble. Eating *before* or *during* drinking does help, because food slows absorption and lowers the peak, but once the alcohol is in your blood, only time removes it.

## How much can you trust this number?

Less than the two decimal places suggest. This deserves a straight answer rather than a disclaimer in small print.

A promille calculator models an average body with an average liver, and then applies that model to you. Real blood alcohol depends on things the arithmetic cannot see: how much and what you ate, whether the drinks were spread over six hours or three, your medication, your liver health, your hydration, and your own metabolic rate. Two people of identical weight and gender, drinking identically, can land meaningfully far apart.

What you *can* rely on is the direction of the error. Relimie's estimator is built so that every uncertain choice pushes the same way, toward a higher reading and a longer wait:

- **No absorption deduction.** Between 10% and 30% of the alcohol you drink is broken down before it ever reaches your bloodstream. The raw Widmark formula ignores that, and so do we. Applying the usual correction would shorten the displayed wait by up to a fifth, exactly in the borderline cases where someone is most likely to act on the number.
- **The whole day counted at once.** Everything you logged is treated as if it hit your blood simultaneously, which produces a higher peak than drinks actually spread across an evening.
- **Durations rounded up.** Every time until clear is rounded up to the next five minutes, never down.
- **No guessed body weight.** Until you enter your weight, the app shows nothing at all rather than assuming a default. An assumed 75 kg would show a *lower* value and a *shorter* wait to anyone lighter than that, which is the one direction this must never err in.

One honest exception: the 0.15 ‰ per hour elimination rate is a mid-range figure, not a cautious one. Real rates run from roughly 0.1 to 0.2 ‰ per hour. If yours is at the slow end, your actual wait is longer than anything shown here, by up to half again.

Which gives a usable verdict: this number is good enough to plan a morning around, and to see that three beers is a longer commitment than it feels like. **It is never good enough to decide whether you can drive, work, operate anything, or take medication.** No calculator is, including this one, and including every app on your phone. If there is any doubt at all, the answer is don't.

## Where Relimie fits in

The weak link in every promille calculator is the input. You have to remember what you drank and how large the pours were, and by the next morning that recall is already unreliable, which is why the estimate is often wrong long before the formula gets involved.

Relimie closes that gap by working from what you logged as you went. You record drinks in the moment, the app converts each one to grams of pure alcohol, and on any day with something logged you can open the estimate directly from your home screen. It shows the level, how it falls hour by hour, and how long until it is fully cleared, from real entries rather than a reconstruction.

> 🎁 **Free, and staying free:** The blood alcohol estimate is part of the free version of Relimie. It is not behind Premium, it never expires with your trial, and it works on any day you logged a drink, including past days. Everything stays on your device, with no account and no cloud.

Over time the same entries feed your [Analytics](index.html#ls-analytics), so the morning-after question turns into something more useful: not just how long until today clears, but what your drinking actually looks like across a month.

## Frequently asked questions

**How much promille do I have after two beers?**
For two 500 ml beers at 5%, that is 40 grams of alcohol. An 80 kg man comes to 40 / (80 × 0.7) = about 0.71 ‰; a 60 kg woman to 40 / (60 × 0.6) = about 1.11 ‰. The same two beers, a difference of more than half a per mille, which is why body weight and gender are not optional inputs.

**How long does it take to clear one per mille?**
At the usual rate of about 0.15 ‰ per hour, roughly six hours and forty minutes. Alcohol leaves at a near constant rate rather than tailing off, so the arithmetic is simply your level divided by 0.15.

**How long does alcohol stay in your system after a long evening?**
Longer than it feels. After 100 grams, roughly five half-litre beers, an 80 kg man is at about 1.79 ‰ and needs close to twelve hours to reach zero. Someone who stopped at two in the morning still has alcohol in their blood at midday, however awake they feel by then.

**Can I speed up sobering up?**
No. Coffee, cold showers, water, food, fresh air and sleep can all make you feel more alert, but none of them change how fast your liver processes alcohol. Only time lowers the level.

**How accurate is a promille calculator?**
Treat it as a range, not a reading. It cannot account for what you ate, how the drinks were spaced, your medication, your liver or your individual metabolism, and real values vary considerably between people who drank exactly the same amount. Relimie's version deliberately rounds toward a higher reading and a longer wait, because that is the only direction that cannot hurt someone acting on it.

**Can I use this to decide whether to drive?**
No, and please don't. This is an estimate produced by arithmetic, not a measurement from a breathalyser or a blood test, and your real level can be considerably higher than what is shown. It is a recovery clock, never a green light. If you are in any doubt, don't drive.

**Does the estimate cost anything in Relimie?**
No. It is part of the free version, it does not expire with your trial, and it is available on every day where you logged at least one drink.

## ARTICLE: Am I Drinking Too Much?

# Am I Drinking Too Much?

"Am I drinking too much?" is one of the most common questions people have about alcohol and their health, and one of the hardest to answer, because "too much" has no single number attached to it. This article can't give you a definitive answer; that would be medical advice, which isn't ours to give. What it can do is point you to a sensible place to start. One of the most useful is comparison: how you stack up against the people around you, and against the guidelines from bodies like the [World Health Organization (WHO)](https://www.who.int).

## First, how much alcohol is in a drink?

Before you can compare anything, it helps to measure the same way. Alcohol is counted in grams of pure alcohol, because a small strong drink and a large weak one can hold exactly the same amount. Here is roughly what common servings contain. Values are approximate and depend on strength and pour.

| Drink | Typical serving | Pure alcohol (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Small glass of wine | 125 ml (12%) | ~12 g |
| Standard glass of wine | 175 ml (12%) | ~17 g |
| Large glass of wine | 250 ml (13%) | ~26 g |
| Bottled beer | 330 ml (5%) | ~13 g |
| Pint of lager or ale | 568 ml (5%) | ~22 g |
| Single spirit | 25 ml (40%) | ~8 g |
| Double spirit | 50 ml (40%) | ~16 g |

So a couple of glasses of wine in an evening is somewhere around 30 to 50 grams of pure alcohol, depending on the size of the pour.

## How much does the average person drink?

An average won't tell you whether your own drinking is fine, but it does give you a reference point, and most people have never actually seen one. Here is the average daily consumption by country, measured in grams of pure alcohol per day. The figures come from national and international data (2026.1).

| Country | Average (men) | Average (women) | Guideline limit (men / women) | Guideline source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Germany | 38.5 g/day | 11.2 g/day | 20 / 10 g/day | DHS/RKI |
| United States | 33.0 g/day | 9.8 g/day | 28 / 14 g/day | USDA |
| United Kingdom | 31.5 g/day | 11.4 g/day | 16 / 16 g/day | NHS |
| Russia | 32.0 g/day | 8.5 g/day | 30 / 20 g/day | Ministry of Health |
| Czechia | 48.0 g/day | 13.5 g/day | 24 / 16 g/day | SZÚ |
| Romania | 54.0 g/day | 14.2 g/day | 24 / 12 g/day | INSP |
| France | 36.0 g/day | 12.5 g/day | 20 / 20 g/day | Santé publique France |

If your country isn't listed, regional averages give a rough stand-in (for example, around 31.5 g/day for men in Europe, or 25.8 g/day in the Americas), so you still have something to compare against.

The codes in the Guideline source column are the national bodies that set each limit: DHS/RKI ([Deutsche Hauptstelle für Suchtfragen](https://www.dhs.de) and the [Robert Koch-Institut](https://www.rki.de)) for Germany, the [USDA](https://www.dietaryguidelines.gov) Dietary Guidelines for the United States, the [NHS](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/alcohol-advice/) (National Health Service) for the United Kingdom, the [Ministry of Health](https://minzdrav.gov.ru) for Russia, [SZÚ](https://szu.cz) (Státní zdravotní ústav) for Czechia, [INSP](https://insp.gov.ro) (Institutul Național de Sănătate Publică) for Romania, and [Santé publique France](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr) for France.

Two useful things stand out. First, the averages are higher than most people guess: 38.5 grams a day for men in Germany is roughly two and a half glasses of wine, every day. Second, in almost every country the average sits *above* the recommended limit, which brings us to the next point.

## Average is not the same as recommended

It is tempting to read an average as a green light, as if drinking "about as much as everyone else" must be fine. But the average describes what is normal, not what is advisable, and the two are often far apart. The right-hand column above shows each country's low-risk guideline, and in most cases the population average is well over it.

The guidelines themselves vary because they are set nationally, not by one global rule. Each limit comes from that country's own health authority, shown in the Guideline source column, not from the WHO. The WHO's own position is blunter still: from a purely health standpoint there is no completely risk-free level of drinking, and less is always lower risk. That is context, not instruction.

## First, find your own average

Here is the catch that trips most people up: you cannot compare a single day against an average. A birthday, a wedding, a Friday night out: of course you drink more than usual on those, and measuring yourself by that one evening tells you nothing. The country figures above are daily averages, so the only fair comparison is your own daily average.

And an average only means something over time. One week is quiet, the next is full of occasions. To reach a figure you can trust, you have to track your drinking over a longer stretch, and a quarter, roughly three months, is a good rule of thumb. Only once the quiet weeks and the heavy ones land in the same pot does a stable personal average emerge, and that is the number worth holding up against the ones in this article.

## Where Relimie fits in

Doing that by hand is tedious, and this is exactly what Relimie is for. You log your drinks as you go, and over the weeks it works out your real daily and weekly average and places it against two lines: the average for people like you, and the recommended guideline. You set a baseline at the start and watch how your actual average settles around it.

> 🎁 **Free baseline comparison:** Relimie sets your baseline from your country's average and shows how your real drinking measures up against it and the guideline, for free, on your device, with no account and no cloud.

Once a few weeks are on screen you can see the trend in your [Analytics](index.html#ls-analytics) and decide what, if anything, you would like to change. You are comparing yourself to a statistic, not to a diagnosis.

## A note on the numbers

These averages are drawn from national and international consumption data, and figures inevitably differ slightly between sources such as the WHO and the [OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development)](https://www.oecd.org), partly because some count every adult and others count only people who actually drink. The guideline limits come from each country's own health authority, shown in the Guideline source column. They are meant as a shared reference point, not a precise personal measurement.

## Frequently asked questions

**How long should I track before I compare?**
Long enough for the busy weeks and the quiet ones to even out. A single night out says nothing about your average, so aim for a longer run: around three months is a sensible benchmark before your personal average is stable enough to hold against the figures here.

**How many grams of alcohol a day counts as "a lot"?**
There is no official line, which is exactly why the question is hard. As a rough guide, many national low-risk guidelines land somewhere between 10 and 20 grams a day, and the WHO holds that less is always lower risk. A practical way to read it: if you are drinking noticeably more than both your country's average and its guideline, you are drinking more than most people around you.

**Is the average amount a safe amount?**
No. An average simply describes what is common, and in most countries the average is already above the recommended limit. Normal and advisable are not the same thing.

**Does Relimie tell me if I drink too much?**
No. Relimie doesn't give medical advice and doesn't diagnose. What it does is statistical: it shows your real intake next to your country's average and its guideline, so the comparison is clear and the conclusions are yours.

## ARTICLE: How Many Calories Are in Alcohol? Wine, Beer & Spirits

# How Many Calories Are in Alcohol? Wine, Beer & Spirits Compared

When we think about what we eat and drink, alcohol is often the part that quietly slips off the list. A glass of wine after work, a beer with friends, a cocktail to round off dinner. These moments matter, and they deserve to be enjoyed. They also carry more calories than most people expect. Knowing the numbers has nothing to do with guilt. It just helps you see the full picture, so the choices you make stay yours.

## The quick answer

Pure alcohol contains about 7 calories per gram, nearly as much as pure fat (9 kcal/g) and almost double the calories in sugar or protein (4 kcal/g). On top of that, many drinks add sugar from mixers, juices and liqueurs.

Here is how common drinks compare. Values are approximate and depend on strength and serving size.

| Drink | Typical serving | Calories (approx.) |
|---|---|---|
| Dry white wine | 175 ml glass (12%) | ~140 kcal |
| Red wine | 175 ml glass (13%) | ~170 kcal |
| Large glass of wine | 250 ml (13%) | ~240 kcal |
| Prosecco or Champagne | 125 ml flute | ~90 kcal |
| Lager or ale | pint / 568 ml (5%) | ~215 kcal |
| Bottled beer | 330 ml (5%) | ~140 kcal |
| Spirit (gin, vodka, whisky) | single 25 ml (40%) | ~55 kcal |
| Gin and tonic | 25 ml plus regular tonic | ~120 kcal |
| Margarita or mixed cocktail | one glass | ~250 to 350 kcal |
| Cream liqueur | 50 ml | ~160 kcal |

## Why alcohol calories are so easy to miss

Nutritionists sometimes call these "empty calories": they give you energy but almost no vitamins, fibre or protein. A few things make them especially easy to overlook.

- Drinks don't feel like food. A pint can carry as many calories as a slice of pizza, but it doesn't register the same way.
- Mixers and cocktails hide sugar. The spirit itself may be modest, while the tonic, juice or syrup often is not.
- One drink leads to a nibble. Alcohol can lower your resolve, so the late-night snack is really part of the same round.

## How quickly it adds up

The individual numbers look small, so it helps to zoom out. Two 175 ml glasses of wine most evenings is roughly 320 calories a day, around 2,200 a week, or close to 9,500 a month. That is the calorie equivalent of a full extra day of eating every week, entirely from drinks.

Seeing that total isn't meant to alarm you. For many people it is simply the missing piece that finally makes their week add up.

## You don't have to quit to take control

You don't need to give up the glass you genuinely enjoy. You just need to see it. When drinks are tracked alongside everything else, moderation stops being a vague intention and becomes something you can actually steer.

That is what Relimie is built for. As you log a drink, it estimates the calories for you, so your evening out is reflected in the same picture as the rest of your day.

> 🎁 **Free calorie tracking:** Relimie estimates the calories in every drink you log. No premium plan, no account, no cloud. Your numbers stay on your device.

Once a week or two of drinks is on the screen, small adjustments become obvious. You can see the trend in your [Analytics](index.html#ls-analytics) and decide what, if anything, you would like to change.

## Five easy ways to cut liquid calories

1. Pour a smaller measure. A 125 ml glass instead of 250 ml halves the calories with barely any difference to the ritual.
2. Reach for a spritzer. Wine topped with soda, or a lower-strength option, keeps the taste and trims the total.
3. Alternate with water. One glass of water between drinks slows the pace and cuts the count.
4. Watch the mixer, not just the spirit. Slimline tonic or soda can save a hundred calories a glass.
5. Track before you trim. You can't adjust what you can't see, and a few logged days usually reveal the easiest win.

## Frequently asked questions

**Which alcohol has the fewest calories?**
Neat spirits with a calorie-free mixer such as soda water or slimline tonic tend to be lowest per serving, around 55 to 60 calories for a single measure. Among wines, a dry white is usually the lightest, thanks to its lower alcohol and minimal residual sugar. A small glass of it, or a light beer, is also relatively modest.

**Does wine or beer have more calories?**
Per glass it is close, but it depends on the pour. A pint of beer usually beats a small glass of wine because the serving is larger. Measure for measure, wine is more calorie-dense because it is stronger.

**Do the calories from alcohol really count?**
Yes. Your body uses the energy from alcohol just as it does from food, and because it burns alcohol first, other calories are more likely to be stored. That is why drinks belong in the picture, not outside it.
